problem: Rounding each share on its own with ROUND_HALF_UP and never handing out the leftover cents means the shares no longer add up to the amount, and the 28-digit decimal context makes large amounts drift too (e.g. '100'/[1,1,1] gives 99.99, '0.05'/[1,1] gives 0.06), so money is lost or created.

Validation goes through _ref.allocate, which uses up a one-shot weights iterable, so line 20 reads nothing and the function returns [] with no error; a re-iterable that changes between reads also gets past validation.
Production code now imports reference_impl and runs the whole reference allocation just for its validation, then throws the result away, which ties the module to the oracle and does the work twice.
The inputs are converted again with Decimal(str(...)) instead of the validated values, so normalisation is lost and Decimal('-0') returns shares of -0.00.
The allocation algorithm was rewritten with no tests covering that the total is kept, the remainder rule, generator weights or places=0, which is how both P1 regressions got in.
Decimal is imported twice (lines 1 and 4) and Fraction on line 2 is no longer used (ruff F811/F401).
The _to_decimal helper is now dead code because nothing calls it.
